title: Dangerous Goods Acceptance: When the Hazardous-Cargo Surcharge Falls Due
content:
## Clause

Loading is the event that brings the Dangerous Goods Acceptance hazardous-cargo surcharge due: when the goods of an acceptance go on board, one surcharge entry is written on that acceptance. Two records show whether this has happened. The acceptance itself must stand as approved or loaded, and the booking carrying the goods must be recorded as loaded, departed or closed. While the booking shows any other status, no surcharge entry is written. An acceptance receives one such entry only; where a hazardous-cargo surcharge entry is already on its account, a second one is not written.

## Status grid

| Acceptance status | Booking status | Existing surcharge entry | Surcharge entry to write |
|---|---|---|---|
| approved or loaded | loaded, departed or closed | none | yes |
| approved or loaded | loaded, departed or closed | present | no |
| approved or loaded | requested, confirmed, equipment released, gated in or cancelled | none | no |
| any other status | any | any | no |

## Points of judgement

**The acceptance still reads approved, but the booking already shows departed.** The surcharge has fallen due; the acceptance status approved is one of the two that allow it.

**The booking shows gated in.** Nothing is written for the moment; gated in is not a loading status.
